A.explanation: Total charge is $(-1/3 -1/3 +2/3)e = 0$, so this is a neutral neutron, not a charged hadron.

B.explanation: Total charge is $(-1/3 +2/3 -1/3)e = 0$, so this combination is neutral and cannot give a charged hadron.

C.explanation: Total charge is $(+2/3 -1/3 -1/3)e = 0$, so this combination is neutral and cannot give a charged hadron.

D.explanation: Total charge is $(+2/3 +2/3 -1/3)e = +1e$, so this gives a hadron with non-zero charge.

hints: Notice the hadron is made of three quarks, so add the three quark charges to get the hadron charge in units of $e$.
Recall the quark charges: up is $+2/3e$, while down and strange are each $-1/3e$.
Test each down-down-up, down-up-strange, up-strange-strange and up-up-strange sum and keep the one that does not sum to zero.
walkthrough: Three quarks together form a baryon, and its charge $Q$ is the sum of the three quark charges.
Use up quark charge $Q_u = +2/3e$, down quark charge $Q_d = -1/3e$ and strange quark charge $Q_s = -1/3e$.
Options A, B and C all sum to zero: A gives $(-1/3 -1/3 +2/3)e = 0$, B gives $(-1/3 +2/3 -1/3)e = 0$, C gives $(+2/3 -1/3 -1/3)e = 0$.
For up, up, strange the sum is $Q = (+2/3 +2/3 -1/3)e = +3/3e = +1e$, which is a charged hadron.
